sourceEvidence.label: GRAF Sparkle signer availability incident and release-tool source review

assessment.summary: One high-leverage custody boundary can eliminate the accidental single local signer without weakening ordinary Sparkle trust continuity.

nonNegotiables: No private key, seed, secret path or secret-bearing log is committed, shipped or published.
Ordinary in-app updates keep the same Sparkle public key and HTTPS feed.
The historic unavailable signer is not treated as recoverable.
Public appcast replacement remains after verified versioned assets.
assumptions: The current owner-only signing channel can use a protected GitHub environment and a controlled macOS Keychain.
No measured release latency or secret-management budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Own Sparkle signer custody behind two protected channels
opportunities.summary: Replace arbitrary local-file/one-Keychain custody with a public manifest, protected GitHub environment signer, Keychain recovery signer, and fail-closed attestations.
opportunities.diagnosis: The release tool correctly validates a selected signer but ownership and recovery live outside a single durable control boundary, allowing availability to depend on one local secret copy.

evidence.claim: The historic private signer is unavailable while installed applications retain its public verifier.
Staging accepts either a Keychain account or arbitrary external private key file and validates only the selected path.
Normal update continuity rejects changed Sparkle public key and feed URL.
Without a versioned public custody declaration and cross-channel attestation, operators cannot prove redundant recovery before a release.

desiredInvariants: Every signer derives the same public key as the active manifest and candidate GRAF app before staging begins.
No regular appcast can change its own feed verifier or feed address.
At least one protected signer remains usable if the other channel is unavailable, while routine readiness visibly reports degraded redundancy.
No secret material crosses the repository, application, public host, artifact, log or diagnostic boundary.

options.title: Retain local Keychain/file custody with stronger documentation
options.summary: Keep the current release helper and ask operators to maintain backups manually.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Documentation cannot recreate the unavailable signer or prove an independent recovery path.
A documented backup policy could reduce accidents but retains arbitrary private-file capability.
Ordinary trust continuity remains correct but does not solve availability.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing signature verification remains, but secret custody stays dispersed and a file fallback remains available.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review releases for use of arbitrary file input and attempt one-channel loss recovery.
Measure existing staging duration as baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new process or retained memory is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No special memory validation beyond existing staging checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: A lost local signer still blocks updates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a loss drill with the only local signer unavailable.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current manual procedure remains familiar but lacks preflight proof of redundancy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Ask an alternate operator to reproduce recovery from docs alone.

tradeoffs.assessment: No client migration occurs, so historic-key clients remain blocked.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm current client cannot validate a new signer.

residualRisks: An arbitrary local key file can be mishandled or leaked.

options.title: Protected GitHub environment signer plus Keychain recovery signer
options.summary: Introduce an active public trust manifest, protected cloud signing workflow, local Keychain fallback, safe cross-channel attestation, and manual bootstrap migration.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A manual bootstrap migrates the unrecoverable historic trust line to a new managed signer.
Local arbitrary-file signing becomes CI-only ephemeral material and local recovery is named Keychain custody.
The strict ordinary update validator remains in place and bootstrap gets a separate explicit path.
Public manifest, attestation and drills make custody ownership/testability explicit.
Focused evidence tests cover no legacy local file signer and fail-closed channel checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: The private key is no longer accepted from arbitrary local files; protected environment access and app/manifest/signer equality create a single auditable release boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise missing/mismatched local and cloud channel cases; scan tracked files and artifacts for key material.

tradeoffs.assessment: Extra derivation and workflow validation occur only during releases, not recording or normal update checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record staging and protected-workflow durations for a representative release.

tradeoffs.assessment: The cloud path uses a short-lived restrictive key file; no long-lived app memory/process is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect workflow cleanup and ensure no cache/artifact contains the file.

tradeoffs.assessment: Either protected channel can sign; normal readiness detects loss of redundancy before a critical release.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run one-channel unavailable drills and a complete two-channel readiness proof.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must manage a protected environment, approval and draft-release workflow, but receive a deterministic readiness/rollback procedure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Have a second approved operator run the quickstart without access to secret values.

tradeoffs.assessment: One manual bootstrap package is necessary for clients bound to the lost historic public key.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove bootstrap plus two sequential normal in-app updates and permission continuity.

residualRisks: If both protected channels are lost, another manual bootstrap is required.
Owner-only code-signing identity remains a separate future migration.

acceptanceCriteria: Both channels attest to one active public key.
Bootstrap then two in-app updates pass.
migrationNotes: Use the first unused CalVer for manual bootstrap and later greater versions for normal updates.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Keep previous signed feed; halt before appcast replacement; fix forward for installed clients.

options.title: Move directly to an external KMS/HSM and public signing program
options.summary: Adopt managed hardware-backed signing, Developer ID and notarization in one broad migration.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A KMS can improve custody but still cannot recover the historic Sparkle key; bootstrap remains necessary.
It can eliminate local-file signing, but requires new provider and certificate workflows.
Code-signing identity migration can affect continuity and must be validated separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: A managed non-exportable signer can reduce private-key export risk, subject to provider design and access policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a separate threat model and provider access review.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote signing adds release latency but not recording runtime cost.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark provider signing during a pilot.

tradeoffs.assessment: No client memory impact is expected.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review client bundle and updater behavior after prototype.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provider availability and account recovery become new dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run outage/recovery drills and audit SLA assumptions.

tradeoffs.assessment: It adds vendor, billing, certificate, notarization and identity-migration operations outside this slice.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Cost and ownership review before selection.

tradeoffs.assessment: Developer ID changes can affect designated requirements and TCC continuity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require a dedicated Spec Kit feature and permission-retention matrix.

residualRisks: Historic trust still needs manual bootstrap.
External service lock-in and code-signing migration risk increase.

workPackages: separate provider selection and Developer ID feature
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remain on the protected dual-custody design until the separate migration is proven.

opportunities.recommendation: Use protected dual custody now; revisit an external KMS/Developer ID migration only after the owner-only release line is stable and a separate permission-continuity plan is approved.

openQuestions: The exact release reviewers and environment policy must be configured by the repository owner before the first physical release.
A future Developer ID/notarization migration needs its own trust and TCC continuity feature.
